role.altitude: The microsystems engineer keeps setting goals, designing concepts, deciding control points and teaching colleagues what the devices do; booking fab time by mail, retyping dates into plans, building checklists from scratch and compiling test data by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Maintaining a control plan as the single source
Using project templates with standard fab durations
role.ambitious_version: An engineer whose plans, checklists and lessons flow from one source of truth.

tasks.short: Define goals and milestones, estimate durations and fab time, book cleanroom tools, build the schedule, agree the plan, and update it to plan and schedule MEMS research or development projects.

steps.what: Engineer defines the project goals, work packages and milestones for the MEMS development projects
Engineer estimates task durations and fabrication run times
Engineer books cleanroom tools and fabrication runs
Engineer builds the schedule in the planning tool
Engineer agrees the plan with the team and management
Engineer updates the schedule as work progresses

tasks.design: A project template holds standard phases, dependencies and typical durations per fabrication step from past projects, and the engineer adjusts them. Cleanroom tools are booked in the tool booking system, which shows availability, instead of mailing the fab coordinators. Booked dates flow into the schedule instead of being typed in again, and completed bookings update progress. Setting goals and agreeing the plan stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Durations were guessed afresh and bookings retyped into the plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Project templates and tool booking systems linked to planning.
tasks.still_hard: New process steps with no history.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which run is likely to fail and planning a spare.
tasks.altitude: Less arranging and retyping; planning choices stay.

evidence.claim: Spreadsheets and mail glue engineering teams today; shared systems replace them.

assumptions: Boundary: planning research and development projects; managing product introduction projects (task 16484) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s3: the cleanroom uses a booking system for about 80% of tools; s3 is priced at that share.
s4 saves the second entry of booked dates into the plan.
Defining goals and agreeing the plan keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of projects planned per year.

incremental.description: Engineer updates standard durations after each project.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: novel processes; high: repeat process flows.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect customer requirements and market data, develop design concepts, estimate performance and cost, write the proposal, and present proposed MEMS product designs.

steps.what: Engineer collects customer requirements and market data
Engineer develops product design concepts
Engineer estimates performance and cost of the concepts
Engineer writes the design proposal document
Engineer presents the proposal to product management and customers

tasks.design: Customer requirements are captured in a requirements register shared with product management, instead of being gathered from mails and meeting notes. The proposal template holds standard sections on process capability and the development path, and the engineer writes the concept and rationale. Developing concepts and presenting stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were scattered and proposals started from old files.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared requirements registers and proposal templates.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which requirement the customer would trade away.

evidence.claim: A requirements and verification tool is used by a grid operator and government without AI.

assumptions: Boundary: proposing designs; investigating cost, performance and process capability (task 16497) and environmental issues (task 19656) are sibling tasks.
s3 is part of investigating cost and performance, which sibling task 16497 covers; its saving is counted there.
Developing concepts and presenting keep their full time.

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the proposal template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off proposals; high: repeat proposals for a product family.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define control points and criteria, write quality assurance guidance and quality control protocols, build process control checklists and data collection forms, set up reporting, and route documents for release.

steps.what: Engineer defines the control points, checks and criteria in the control plan
Engineer writes quality assurance guidance and quality control protocols

loop.input: The control plan and the procedure template.
loop.output: Draft protocol text per control point.
loop.check: Every criterion, limit and frequency in the text must match the control plan; any mismatch stops the draft; the engineer edits each section.
loop.stop: The engineer writes the section by hand after two failed checks.
loop.why_not_simpler: Protocol wording differs per process step.

steps.what: Engineer builds process control checklists and data collection forms
Engineer sets up reporting of the collected data
Engineer routes the documents for review and release

tasks.design: The control plan is the single source: checklists and electronic data collection forms are generated from it, and a drafting step writes protocol text per control point with every criterion matched to the plan. A report template links to the data forms. The document control workflow routes the documents for review and release, instead of mail. Defining the control points stays with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protocols, checklists and forms were written separately and drifted apart.
tasks.enabler_now: Control plans that generate checklists and forms, and digital validation tools.
tasks.still_hard: Processes still being developed, where the plan changes weekly.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the few checks that actually catch defects.
tasks.altitude: Less writing the same thing three times; deciding controls stays.

evidence.claim: A drug maker cut validation cycle time by over 50% across 27 sites with digital protocols and records; vendor case, no method.
In a writing experiment with 453 professionals, not engineers, a model cut time by 40% and raised quality by 18%.

assumptions: Boundary: QA and QC documentation; product test protocols and acceptance thresholds (task 16501) and SPC validation (task 16507) are sibling tasks.
s3 saves building checklists and forms separately from the plan.
Defining control points keeps its full time.
unknowns: Number of documents per process flow.
research_questions: Do checklist and protocol mismatches fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: processes still changing; high: stable flows with many control points.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile test and field performance data, interpret lessons, write a lessons note, and communicate operating characteristics or performance experience to engineers or designers in reviews or training.

steps.what: Engineer compiles test results and field performance data
Engineer interprets the operating characteristics and lessons learned
Engineer writes the lessons-learned note
Engineer communicates performance experience to engineers and designers in reviews or training
Engineer answers follow-up questions

tasks.design: A dashboard on the test database and field-return records shows performance per device type and condition, instead of the engineer compiling exports. The lessons-learned template has fixed sections and links to the data. Interpreting and teaching stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test and field data were compiled by hand for each review.
tasks.enabler_now: Test databases and field-return records in one dashboard.
tasks.still_hard: Field failures reported only in customer mails.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a device behaves differently in the field than in the lab.

reach.learn: Whether known failure modes are designed out.

evidence.claim: Test data and root cause work suit dashboards and statistics.

assumptions: Boundary: communicating performance experience; failure and reliability analyses (task 16505) and customer documentation (task 16488) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: test results and field returns recorded in the databases, for about 70% of devices; s1 is priced at that share.
Interpreting, presenting and answering keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of field returns recorded in the system.
research_questions: Are lessons reused in new designs?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: field data in mails; high: field returns and tests in databases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
